findings.message: OfferController queries are not tenant-scoped
findings.impact: A user with access to the offers feature may receive records or aggregate counts belonging to other tenants.
findings.remediation: Apply active-tenant scoping consistently to list, count and status aggregate queries. Verify tenant ownership across joined records.
findings.verification_basis: Source inspection of controller queries and route middleware.
evidence: The index query joins offers, applications, candidates and vacancies without a tenant predicate.
The count query uses the same unscoped conditions.
The status count aggregates all non-deleted offers without tenant filtering.
The route permission controls access to the feature but does not scope records to the active tenant.

findings.message: PersonHiredHandler does not validate tenant ownership of payload entities
findings.impact: An event payload containing mismatched or foreign entity identifiers may create an employee record with invalid cross-tenant relationships.
findings.remediation: Resolve the tenant from trusted execution context and validate person and candidate ownership and their relationship before insertion.
findings.verification_basis: Source inspection of event handler lookup and insert logic.
evidence: The handler reads tenant_id, person_id and candidate_id from the event payload.
The duplicate employee lookup checks person_id globally without tenant scoping.
The handler inserts the supplied identifiers without validating their tenant ownership or relationships.

findings.message: Event worker does not hold a transaction around SKIP LOCKED selection
findings.impact: Concurrent workers may select the same pending events and execute listeners more than once.
findings.remediation: Implement an atomic transactional claim-and-process strategy, with explicit commit and rollback boundaries.
findings.verification_basis: Source inspection of EventBus and Database transaction/query methods.
evidence: processPending selects pending events using FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.
The method does not begin a transaction before selecting rows.
Database::select executes the query and fetches results without establishing a transaction.
Under normal PDO autocommit behavior, row locks are released when the SELECT statement completes.

findings.message: EventBus executes dispatched events synchronously while leaving them pending
findings.impact: Listeners may execute a second time when the worker later processes the same pending event.
findings.remediation: Choose a consistent delivery model. For an outbox model, dispatch should persist the event and let the worker execute it, with idempotent listener handling.
findings.verification_basis: Source inspection of dispatch and processPending behavior.
evidence: dispatch inserts the event into the outbox with pending status.
dispatch then executes registered listeners synchronously.
The event remains pending for subsequent processing by the CLI worker.

findings.message: CLI event worker does not register module listeners
findings.impact: Events requiring module listeners may be marked completed without their intended business logic executing.
findings.remediation: Provide a dedicated module listener registration bootstrap for CLI workers without unnecessarily repeating web bootstrap side effects.
findings.verification_basis: Source inspection of CLI worker, ModuleRegistrar, HR Module and EventBus listener execution.
evidence: The CLI worker constructs EventBus and calls processPending.
It does not boot the application or invoke ModuleRegistrar.
The HR module registers PersonHiredHandler through its register method.
ModuleRegistrar boot is the discovered mechanism that invokes module registration.
The worker can therefore process events with an empty listener registry and mark them completed.
